description: Constitutional principles for autonomous code self-critique

security.rule: No hardcoded secrets, API keys, or passwords
All user inputs must be validated before use
No eval() or exec() with dynamic content
No SQL string concatenation — use parameterized queries
No shell injection via unquoted variables in commands

error_handling.rule: No empty catch blocks — all errors must be handled or re-thrown
Error messages must be descriptive — no generic 'Error occurred'
error_handling.check: grep -niE '(error occurred|something went wrong|an error happened)' {file}

error_handling.rule: Return values from commands must be checked
No silent failures — failed operations must log or propagate errors

quality.rule: No TODO/FIXME/HACK comments in production code
No magic numbers — use named constants
No duplicate code blocks over 10 lines
No console.log or print statements left in production code

testing.rule: New functions must have corresponding tests
Tests must cover error and edge cases, not just happy path
No test-only code in production files
Test assertions must be specific — no assertTrue(result) without message

performance.rule: All database queries must have .limit() or LIMIT clause
No unbounded loops over external data
Avoid synchronous file I/O in hot paths
